answer: Each agent’s influence can be tied to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is locked before it votes and forfeited if a later audit proves coordinated fraud. A newcomer may enter through an inlet and whisper claims, but cannot multiply voting weight merely by minting identities: every Sybil account needs its own stake, while detection burns the attackers’ deposits. This makes a fake-identity campaign costly in capital and exposes funds to loss, rather than relying on names or reputation alone to harbor trust.
